forcedChoices.choice: «tu interpretación» (singular), with «de qué han estado hablando» (plural)
forcedChoices.reason: Jesus speaks to Peter, and Peter answers with the interpretation he himself decided upon (151:2.2); the talk was the group's.

forcedChoices.choice: the servants address the householder with «usted»
forcedChoices.reason: They call him 'Sir' and 'master'; the English shows respect to one person of higher station.
Spanish imperative forces singular or plural; the English 'be quiet' can address Peter alone or all of them, so the noun keeps both readings open.
«maligno» is the glossary form for 'the evil one'; «malos» avoids the same form for a different term.
The glossary gives 'prince of devils' as «príncipe de los demonios»; «diablo» is kept for 'the devil' (Caligastia).
